A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReNF study and contain the main text, equations, experimental tables, figures, and Appendices A–H. Text extraction, visual inspection, and matching figure content support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original ReNF forecasting results, ablations, training analyses, and oracle forecast-combination experiments in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains the original forecasting experiments, ablations, uncertainty analysis, and prediction visualizations, with limited numerical revisions.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same ReNF alpha/beta architectures, recursive BDO concatenation, normalization and dropout, weighted time/frequency loss, and EMA evaluation procedure. The theoretical terminology changes do not alter the method.

E1.justification: Reported evaluations retain ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, ETTm2, Weather, Electricity, Solar, and Traffic. The forecasting tasks, represented domains, and test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 7 retain the same nine main baselines. Table 6 retains TimeBridge, OLinear, TQNet, and CARD. The newly cited forecast-combination works are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Both retain the same dataset splits, MSE/MAE metrics, four forecast horizons, look-back search over 336/512/720, Timer-XL's 672-length input, and supplementary fixed-96 protocol. No training or evaluation settings are revised.

E4.justification: The EMA, BDO-versus-DO, depth, oracle-bound, pre-dropout, two-component, and architecture-swap analyses are retained. The representation and prediction visualizations also match; appendix reflow does not add or remove analyses.

E5.justification: Both specify seed 2021 for the main experiments. Table 9 retains the same five-run analysis with different seeds, standard deviations, and 99% confidence entries; uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Under the unchanged fixed-96 look-back setting, Table 6 revises ReNF's Weather MAE from 0.242 to 0.243 at horizon 192, from 0.284 to 0.285 at horizon 336, and from 0.265 to 0.266 on average. This removes its reported average-MAE tie with CARD at 0.265. Other results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 becomes Proposition 1, but its mathematical statement, assumptions A1–A4, bound, and Appendix C proof remain unchanged. The definitions and Appendix D loss derivation also match; relabeling introduces no mathematical revision.

C1.justification: V1 claims a theoretical foundation that 'rigorously demonstrates' the value of multiple forecasters; v3 presents a principle providing 'formal motivation'. This modestly narrows the theoretical contribution while retaining the BDO, EMA, efficiency, and performance claims.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 adds an explicit diverse-estimator ensemble interpretation. Appendix A narrows the bagging analogy from collaborative training plus post-combination to collaborative training alone. Existing oracle-bound caveats and applicability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Hardware, Adam optimization, hyperparameter ranges, preprocessing, and dataset documentation are unchanged. The code-access placeholders in the abstract and reproducibility statement remain empty in both PDFs.

R1.justification: V3 adds Bates and Granger (1969), Clemen (1989), Zhang's hybrid forecasting work (2003), and N-BEATS (Oreshkin et al., 2019). A new Appendix A paragraph and Section 2.2 passage connect ReNF to classical forecast combination and distinguish its internal recursive combination from parallel forecasters.

P1.justification: Edits concentrate on the abstract, first contribution, theoretical headings and terminology, and the added related-work paragraph. Section order and most prose remain intact; this is a localized revision.

P2.justification: Figure 1's caption changes MNFT to MNFP. Table 6 removes ReNF's erroneous red emphasis for Weather average MAE and marks CARD's value blue. Added text causes limited appendix reflow; the figure and table inventory and graphical content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V3 improves claim calibration by presenting the theoretical contribution as motivation, adds clearer forecast-combination context, and corrects misleading Table 6 ranking emphasis. These are limited improvements: the method, proof, and experimental support remain unchanged, and Section 2.5 still retains the old MNFT terminology.
